steps.label: Liveness check
WCSPH (same regime as 50_couple_rigid_fluid_oneway.json)
Effect length 0.6 = one seed spacing
Pressure coe scale (WCSPHFluid::estimatePressureCoe(0.6, 98.0))
Rest density
Particle radius 0.3 = seed spacing 0.6, which puts seeds on x=0/z=0 and therefore inside ScenePreset::BoxDrop's 1x1x1 drop column (docs/issue/CODEBASE_ISSUES.md 1.7)
Shallow pool, x/z in [-1.2,1.2], y in [0,1.2]
Container: floor at y=0, walls just outside the pool, open top
Floor + box dropping from y=3
Negative baseline: coupling disabled entirely
Rebuild fluid+rigid, uncoupled
Precondition: coupling reports disabled
Precondition: 5x3x5 seeded pool
Pool settles onto the floor while the box is still above it
Reference sample taken before the box could reach the pool either way -- the coupled pass below has to reproduce this exactly
The box passes straight through the pool's position: with no boundary registered for it the fluid never feels it, and simply keeps settling (~0.6s)
Uncoupled: the pool is quietly settling, nothing has disturbed it
Uncoupled: the box occupies the same volume as the fluid, because nothing pushed the fluid out of it
Comparison run: same scene, coupling enabled One-Way
Enable Rigid-Fluid coupling
One-Way (SDF penalty on fluid)
Rebuild fluid+rigid+bindings
One-Way confirmed active
Same 40 steps as the baseline run
Precondition: while the box is still clear of the pool the two runs are bit-for-bit identical -- so any divergence past this point is the coupling and nothing else
Box plunges through the pool, now pushed out of its way by the box's SDF penalty

Change: the pool is being actively stirred, orders of magnitude above the undisturbed baseline. This is the suite's proof that One-Way coupling reaches the solver; note the original form of this check sampled GetMaxParticlePositionY instead, which is dominated by a rim particle the box never touches and reads identical either way.

Diagnostic: the penalty has pushed fluid out of the volume the box now occupies, so the pool's centre of mass sits a little below the uncoupled run's (~0.475 vs ~0.494). Only the range is asserted here -- that 4% gap is too small to hang the scenario's contract on, which is why speed_oneway/speed_uncoupled is what post_assert compares.
Let the box finish settling on the floor (~0.5s more)
Invariant: fluid stays bounded (no explosion)
Invariant: fluid rests on the floor (no penetration beyond numerical slop)
Invariant: box (body 1) reaches the floor regardless of coupling (One-Way never pushes back on the box)
Invariant: particle count conserved
